The estate can most likely recover the injury-related damages: medical and ambulance costs, lost earnings from the accident until death, and pain and suffering before death. It can also recover funeral costs and wrongful-death damages for her dependants, such as lost support and companionship. The driver will argue that her refusal of the transfusion was a superseding cause or an unreasonable failure to mitigate, which could bar or reduce the death-related damages, but because the refusal rests on a sincerely held religious belief, most courts treat it as reasonable and not superseding. This assumes a common-law system such as the US or England, and the answer varies by jurisdiction.
